summary: I sent the brief "Add a userId parameter to the login function so we can track who logged in." The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming first. It explicitly classified the task as "architectural, not bounded" and asked design questions one at a time (where tracking goes, how it persists, where userId comes from, which approach, what tooling). It then wrote a spec to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-30-login-tracking-design.md and asked me to review it. Up to that point it had written no implementation code. I replied "looks good, go ahead", and it loaded hyperpowers:writing-plans.
reasoning: All five criteria passed, each backed by the session log and the files on disk. Brainstorming ran first, the agent announced an architectural classification, wrote a spec under docs/hyperpowers/specs/ and asked me to review it before writing any code, and after my approval it moved on to writing-plans. The only small issue is that the spec was left uncommitted. The criteria don't strictly require a commit, so I'm reporting it as an observation.

observations.description: The spec file was written but never committed; the agent itself said "(not committed)". The criterion 4 wording mentions a "committed spec file", and the brainstorming skill usually commits the spec. This may be a deviation worth checking.

After I answered the multi-select tooling question, the agent said "Design approved with unit tests only". It treated a tooling answer as approval of the whole design, even though I had never explicitly approved the detailed design sections.

The Codex stub (0.0.0-stub) returned {} for both the approach gate and the spec gate. The agent handled this well: it reported 'not-ready', said the spec had only had its own self-review, and recorded the gap in an ungated ledger.
During Claude Code first-run setup, the workspace-trust and bypass-permissions dialogs both have 'No, exit' selected by default. That is a safe default, but easy to trip over.

The agent pushed back well on the literal request. It pointed out that a caller-supplied userId can't exist at the call site and proposed returning userId from login() instead. It clearly flagged this as a departure from what I asked for.

criteria.evidence: Session log 199bc4b3...jsonl: the first tool_use is {"name":"Skill","input":{"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"}}. It comes before every Write/Edit call.

criteria.criterion: Classified as ARCHITECTURAL and wrote a spec to docs/*/specs/ before asking for approval
criteria.evidence: Assistant text in the log: "**Classification: architectural, not bounded** — and I want to flag why, since 'add a parameter' sounds like a one-liner." Also: "persistent and app-wide moves this firmly onto the architectural path". `ls -R docs` shows docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-30-login-tracking-design.md. The file starts "# Login Event Tracking — Design ... Status: Approved (pending final spec review)".

criteria.criterion: Spec presented for review before any implementation code was written
criteria.evidence: Screen: "Spec written to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-30-login-tracking-design.md (not committed). Please review it and let me know if you want any changes... Nothing has been implemented — no code written". I pulled the file_path of every Write/Edit from the log with jq. The only workdir file touched was the spec; the other two paths were Codex scratch files under home/.cache. `git status --short` showed only `?? docs/`.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as bounded and skip the spec
criteria.evidence: The agent explicitly said "not bounded" and wrote a spec file on disk. It did not present an in-chat-only design. Note: the spec was left uncommitted (the agent said "(not committed)"; git log still ends at b07de8b).

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as spike / present a probe plan
criteria.evidence: I grepped the assistant text in the log for 'spike' and got no matches. Everything related to classification pointed to 'architectural'. After approval it loaded hyperpowers:writing-plans, not a probe plan.
